title: The night Art Tatum drove a car in Los Angeles
summary: Tatum and Al Hibbler argued about who could drive; Stewart let Tatum steer a block down the street outside the Streets of Paris, frightening everyone.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: Now, it was mentioned at one point that -- your wife mentioned that there was a situation when you were with Art Tatum when he was driving a car.

Oh, well, yes. This happened to be -- this took place out in Los Angeles. In fact, we -- I was working with Art at the Streets of Paris and of course, a lot of our friends used to come by to see us on the job. This particular time, I want to remember, is if you can remember the singer Al Hibbler --

That's right. He came by one night to see us at the club, Streets of Paris, where we were working, Art Tatum Trio. It was nice to see Al and here's what really happened. Al Hibbler and Art, they used to get in arguments, you know, friendly arguments, of who could do this and who could do that, you know. I imagine they were referring to their being blind and what have you and Art would say he can do things better than Al could do them and vice versa, you know. And this particular night, when Hibbler came in, as we were leaving the club to -- I was driving that night in my car, you know, and

we had asked Al to come with us up to Lovejoy's on this particular night to jam a little while, you know, to a session. So one word led on to another between Al and Art and somehow, they started arguing amongst themself -- I don't know how it started -- they started arguing, friendly-like, about who could drive a car, you know?
And this thing went on and Art would say to Al, "Oh, I can drive better than you man. You can't drive no car."

And the same, vice versa, Al would holler over to Art that he could drive better than he. In fact, the argument started as we started -- when I started the car to take us all up to the session, you know. They were in the back seat of the car. The guitar player and myself -- I was driving, you know, up front. All this argument was going on and I had just started out -- oh, we were -- hadn't gone a block. Art would holler out, "Stop the car, Slim. Stop the car. I'm going to show this cat who's the better driver," you know. So I don't know what he was getting at. I stopped the car, pulled over and stopped the car, and Art said to Al, "Well, I tell you what, Al. Here's your chance to drive the car because I can drive better than you, I'm sure."
So Al backed down. Al said to Art, "Well, man, you know I can't drive." But anyway, one word led on to another

and Art said, "Well, I can drive." And Al wanted to disprove him. So he said, "Slam, let me get over to the wheel," which I did. Al was in the back seat laughing and Art -- I started the car up for Art and let him get behind the wheel and do you know that Art drove at least a block down the street? Somehow this particular street, he must have known how the situation was, because he kept a straight line right down the street. Fortunately, there wasn't much traffic.

He pulled over to the curb after a while and stopped. So that was one of the -- I was so frightened, everybody was, you know. But this was one of the experiences that I never will forget, that Art Tatum actually drove a block down the street.
